links.outcome: Comprehension of safety-relevant discharge information: GPT-4 patient-centered letters versus standard discharge letters
links.effect: OR 1.74 (95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001). Learning objectives fully stated 45.7% vs 38.5%; omissions 24.3% vs 34.8%. Gains were largest for medication and organization, smaller for higher-order understanding.
links.quote: The letter type significantly influenced comprehension (odds ratio [OR] 1.74, 95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001).

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM to convert clinician discharge letters into patient-centered versions to reduce cognitive load and improve retention

screen.reason: Prospective crossover study evaluating the impact of GPT-4-generated patient-centered discharge letters versus standard discharge letters on standardized patients' comprehension of discharge information.
